summary: Backend-only re-test after refactor: per-vegetable product model with 4 categories (cut-veg, cut-fruit, whole, ready-mix), available_cuts/available_weights arrays, and Stripe via emergentintegrations. Rewrote/expanded pytest suite to 30 cases covering health, products (v3 schema + all 4 categories + available_cuts multi-value + cut_type filter against available_cuts array), pincodes (serviceable/non), auth (register/login/me/dup/wrong-pw/no-token + admin login), orders (auth-req, bad-pincode, create+GET verify, list-my), Stripe (checkout returns url+session_id, status endpoint returns paid/payment_status/status fields), admin RBAC (401/403 on POST product, POST/DELETE pincode, DELETE product), and admin CRUD with new schema fields. Result: 30/30 PASS (100%). All 12 requested scenarios verified end-to-end. Stripe now succeeds via emergentintegrations with sk_test_emergent — session_id and Stripe hosted URL returned. Seeded product count = 33 as expected.

minor.issue: Stripe rejects amounts below its $0.50 minimum. Order totals below ~₹48 (e.g. one Baby Spinach @ ₹39) will fail with 'total amount must convert to at least 50 cents'. Not a bug in our code, but recommend either (a) enforcing a minimum cart total server-side for stripe payment_method, or (b) surfacing this Stripe error to the UI cleanly instead of 500.

action_items: (Optional/minor) Enforce a server-side minimum order total (~₹50) when payment_method='stripe' in POST /api/orders or POST /api/payments/checkout to avoid raw Stripe 500 for very small carts.
(Optional) Migrate deprecated FastAPI @app.on_event('startup') to lifespan context manager (works today, but deprecated).
(Optional) server.py is ~490 lines — still under the 700 threshold but consider splitting into routers (auth/products/pincodes/orders/payments) as it grows.

(Optional/security) Order creation trusts client-supplied items[].price and delivery_fee/subtotal/total. A malicious client could set price=0. Consider revalidating from db.products + db.pincodes server-side before persisting.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py:339 wraps Stripe SDK exceptions as HTTP 500 with raw provider text. Consider mapping known Stripe errors (min amount, invalid currency) to 400.
Order model persists total/subtotal from client; no server-side recomputation — see action items.
Product model uses Literal for category (good), but cut_type is free-form str. Consider Literal or Enum for consistency across available_cuts.
No rate-limiting / brute-force protection on /api/auth/login and /api/auth/register.
updated_files: /app/backend/tests/test_freshcuts_api.py (rewritten for v3 schema + emergentintegrations Stripe; added ready-mix, cut-fruit, whole tests + available_cuts filter test + Stripe /payments/status test)
seed_data_creation: None manually created. Startup reseeder produced 33 products at SEED_VERSION=3 as expected. Admin user + 8 pincodes seeded on first boot. Test users are per-session with TEST_ prefix; test-created products/pincodes are cleaned up in their tests.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Backend base URL from frontend/.env EXPO_PUBLIC_BACKEND_URL. Admin creds: admin@freshcuts.com / Admin@123. Pydantic EmailStr rejects reserved TLDs — use real-looking domains. Stripe now uses emergentintegrations and works with sk_test_emergent; keep test amounts >= ~₹50 to stay above Stripe's $0.50 min. cut_type filter matches against available_cuts array (not the scalar cut_type field).
rca_of_issue: Previous iteration's only failure (Stripe 500 with placeholder key) is resolved by switching to emergentintegrations.payments.stripe.checkout.StripeCheckout, which accepts sk_test_emergent. Confirmed via TestStripeCheckout: POST /api/payments/checkout returns {url, session_id} (200); GET /api/payments/status/{session_id} returns {paid, payment_status, status, order_id} (200).
